D021-D022_h001.question: "Well, doctor, it's been a while now, probably close to six months, that food has become... a real trouble. I'm 74, a widow, and honestly, retirement should be peaceful. But I find myself avoiding so many things. Carbs, fats, it all feels wrong. If it's not a vegetable, I question if I should eat it. I keep an eye on the scale constantly. Every morning, first thing, I step on it, and if it's even a little higher, my day is ruined. I just can't stand the thought of gaining an ounce. Sometimes, mind you, I just can't stop eating, especially when I'm alone and feeling low. I'll eat until I feel utterly stuffed, and then, well, I just feel so ashamed and disgusted with myself that I find ways to get rid of it. I know it's not right, but the thought of keeping all that food in me, and what it might do to my weight, it's just unbearable."
D021-D022_h001.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder
D021-D022_h001.answer: B & A. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h002.question: Honestly, Doc, I don't know what’s going on, but it's been a few months now, maybe four or five. The kitchen is always intense, and I used to thrive on it, but lately, I'm just drained. I’ve started skipping meals a lot, especially breakfast and sometimes even lunch during service. It’s easier to just push through. I've been watching the scale closely, and yeah, the numbers keep dropping. It's a weird feeling, seeing that, and I can't shake the anxiety that comes with seeing it creep up even a little. I’ll admit, sometimes I eat a ton, way more than I should, and then… well, I hate that feeling, so I get rid of it. I just want to feel like myself again, not constantly thinking about food and my weight. My wife's noticed something's off, too; she’s worried.
D021-D022_h002.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder
D021-D022_h002.answer: B & A. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h003.question: I'm not sure where to start, honestly. Lately, I’ve just been so preoccupied with what I eat. I’ve cut out anything with carbs or fats completely; I just keep thinking about how much healthier I'll be. It's been a few months now, and I’ve really dropped a lot of weight. Every time I look at a slice of pizza or a burger, I just see myself gaining it all back instantly. I’ve never really considered myself overweight, but I know I need to be careful. Sometimes, the hunger just gets to be too much, and I end up eating a ridiculous amount, then I just feel disgusted with myself and have to get rid of it. As a vet, I’m on my feet all day, and I need my energy, but this constant fear of certain foods is draining.
D021-D022_h003.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder
D021-D022_h003.answer: B & A. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h004.question: I’m a 29-year-old investment banking analyst, and for the past few months, things have felt… off. It started subtly, maybe around six months ago. I’ve always been driven, but this feels different. I find myself intentionally skipping meals—breakfast is often out of the question and lunch usually gets pushed aside for work. When I do eat, I find myself worrying constantly about how much I'm consuming, followed by an urge to just get rid of it. I'll make myself throw up right after those meals. It's not every time, but it happens frequently enough that I've noticed a pattern. I'm afraid to gain weight; in fact, the idea of not being lean terrifies me. I just want to lose more, even though my friends and family comment that I look thin. But I know I could lose more.
D021-D022_h004.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder
D021-D022_h004.answer: B & A. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h005.question:
It’s…it’s been hard, you know? Residency is a grind. I used to love food, but lately, it's just a source of anxiety. I find myself eating really small amounts, maybe just a few bites at each meal, if that. I’m always aiming to drop a few more pounds, even though I know I’m already pretty light. The thought of eating something "unhealthy"—anything high-calorie, really—just fills me with dread. I'm convinced it’ll instantly make me gain weight.

There are days, though, when the hunger just gets to me, especially after a brutal shift. I'll find myself eating a lot, quickly, and then… I feel so disgusted and guilty. So I do things to get rid of it. I know it’s probably not healthy, but it helps me feel a bit more in control. This has been going on for a few months now, and honestly, I just feel exhausted all the time.
D021-D022_h005.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Adjustment Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder
D021-D022_h005.answer: B & A. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h006.question: "Well, doctor, it all started a few months after my Helen passed. I just… stopped feeling hungry, you know? It's been tough, navigating this house alone after all these years. I barely eat, a little bit here, a little bit there. I try to keep it under 500 calories most days. My clothes are all loose, and I’m definitely lighter than I used to be, but I don’t mind. Some days I get lightheaded, or my hair seems thinner, but I just chalk that up to getting older, really. Sometimes, though, I just can't stop myself. I’ll eat and eat until I feel sick, and then… well, I usually have to bring it all back up. It’s a bit of a relief afterwards, I suppose. I don’t think much of it, just a habit I’ve fallen into."
D021-D022_h006.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D021-D022_h006.answer: C & D. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h007.question: Lately, flying just zaps all my energy. I’ve been so careful about what I eat, really watching every single thing that goes into my body. It’s been… I don’t know, a few months now, that I’ve been so particular. I feel like I’m constantly losing weight, and I see it, but I don’t think it’s a big deal. People tell me I look thin, but honestly, I feel fine, even when I sometimes get a bit lightheaded. Then, sometimes, after being so good, I just lose control and eat a huge amount, way more than I intend to. And afterwards, I feel so guilty and disgusted that I end up trying to get rid of it. I just want to feel like I have some control, you know? My uniform feels a bit looser, which is good, but the exhaustion is getting hard to hide from my colleagues.

A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D021-D022_h007.answer: C & D. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h008.question: "Well, doctor, it's been a few months now, maybe five or six, that things have felt… off. My wife, she’s noticed it too. I've found myself just not eating. I'll skip breakfast, then lunch will just sort of pass me by. Dinner, I try to eat with her, but often I just pick at it. It's not that I don't like food, it's just… I don't feel I need as much. I’ve started trying to shed a few pounds, felt like I was getting a bit soft around the middle, even though everyone says I’m thin enough already. I know sometimes I feel a bit light-headed, and my hair seems a bit thinner, but I just put it down to getting older and working long hours. Sometimes, honestly, I just can’t help myself and end up eating a huge amount, way more than I intend, and then I just feel disgusted with myself and try to get rid of it. But then I tell myself I need to be more disciplined."

    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bulimia Nervosa

I just want to get down to my ideal weight, and I think I'm almost there. When they bring it up, I just tell them they're overreacting. Sometimes, though, I just can't stop myself. I'll eat a huge amount, really quickly, and then I feel so guilty afterward, I just… get rid of it. I know it's not healthy, but I can't seem to stop the cycle.

    C. Anorexia Nervosa

D021-D022_h010.question: "It's been a rough few months, maybe six or so. I just don't feel like eating most of the time. Breakfast is a write-off, and by lunch, I'm just not hungry, so I usually skip it. Dinner's hit or miss. I’ve dropped a few pounds, and honestly, I feel better for it, lighter, like I can move around easier. My wife keeps saying I look thin, but I think I could stand to lose a bit more. Sometimes, though, I get these moments where I just can't stop eating, like I’m in a tunnel. After that, I just feel… dirty, you know? And I try to get rid of it. I know it sounds a bit odd, and I have felt a bit lightheaded sometimes, especially during my shifts, but I just push through it. It's nothing a bit of water can't fix, or just sitting down when I get a chance. My hair’s been a bit thinner, too, but I’m getting on a bit, so I figure that’s just age."

    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h011.question: "It's been... I don't know, about eight or nine months now, maybe a bit longer actually. I started just trying to eat a bit healthier, you know, for my blood pressure and all, working a desk job at City Hall isn't exactly high-intensity. But it quickly turned into something more. I’m meticulously tracking every single thing I put in my mouth, trying to keep the numbers as low as possible. My wife, she’s worried because I seem to be constantly losing weight, but honestly, when I look in the mirror, I just see a bigger version of myself. My stomach, my thighs… sometimes, after I've eaten, I feel so disgusted with myself, like I’ve completely lost control. I’ll go to the bathroom and try to get rid of it. I know it’s not normal, this constant focus on my weight, but I just can't shake the feeling that I need to be smaller, thinner."
D021-D022_h011.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D021-D022_h012.question:
Alright, doc, thanks for seeing me. It's… well, it’s been a rough few months, probably pushing six by now, maybe longer. I just feel like I'm losing control. The gavel used to feel natural, but now... it's like my whole day revolves around what I'm eating, or, more accurately, what I'm *not* eating. I've cut back so much, down to almost nothing some days. A good day at the auction house, making a sale, closing a deal – it all feels completely meaningless if I haven't kept my calories in check. That's the real measure for me, you know? How much I’ve managed to restrict.

My wife, she’s noticed I’ve lost some weight, keeps asking if I’m eating properly. And I tell her I am, but then sometimes... sometimes I just can't stop myself. I'll eat a ton, feel completely disgusted, and then I just have to get rid of it. The thought of gaining an ounce, even from one slip-up, is terrifying. I *have* to get to a certain weight, a really low weight, and I just can't seem to get there. It’s a constant battle, and honestly, I just feel exhausted.
D021-D022_h012.options:
A. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D021-D022_h012.answer: D & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h013.question: "It's been… I don't know, about eight or nine months now, maybe more, where things just feel out of control. I've become incredibly particular about what I eat. Every time I look in the mirror, my thighs, my stomach, they just seem so much larger than they should be, even though logically I know I've been losing weight pretty consistently. D021-D022_h014.question: I’m not really sure why I’m here. My friends, they keep saying I look too thin, but honestly, I still see a lot of areas I need to work on. I’ve been trying to eat less, just a few bites here and there, and sometimes I'll even skip a meal or only eat once a day. I’ve lost a noticeable amount of weight over the last few months, and it just keeps going down. D021-D022_h015.question: "I’ve just been so preoccupied with what I eat lately. I've cut out all carbs and most fats, strictly, really focusing on 'clean' foods, you know? D021-D022_h016.question: It’s been a rough few months, doctor. Ever since my husband passed, I've had trouble with my appetite. I find myself skipping meals more often than not – breakfast just feels… unnecessary, and sometimes lunch slips by too. I’ve definitely lost weight, not that I’m complaining, but my clothes are looser than they used to be, and not just a little. I’ve become awfully particular about what I eat, terrified that even a small bite of something "unhealthy" will just balloon me up. I’m scared to gain any weight back. D021-D022_h017.question:
"I'm here because… well, things just feel off. It's been going on for about six months now, maybe a bit longer. My trading success hinges on absolute control and discipline, and that mentality started bleeding into other areas, especially food. I've been really rigid about what I eat, meticulously tracking every single calorie. I barely allow myself anything, maybe a few hundred calories a day, just to stay sharp for the market.

And the weight… it just keeps dropping. I try not to think about the numbers too much, but I can feel it. Clothes are looser, and honestly, a part of me gets a sick satisfaction from it. The idea of gaining even a single pound, of getting soft or losing that edge, it absolutely terrifies me. Sometimes, though, the control just snaps. I’ll end up eating a huge amount of food, way more than I intend to, and afterwards, I get so disgusted with myself that I find myself looking for ways to undo it, like forcing myself to throw up. It’s a vicious cycle."

    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bulimia Nervosa
D021-D022_h017.answer: C & D. Anorexia Nervosa & Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h018.question: "I've been meticulously tracking everything I eat for the past six months, probably even longer. It started subtly, but now... I panic if a calorie count is too high. I just can't bring myself to eat certain things anymore, especially anything I perceive as 'heavy.' The thought of gaining even a pound from those foods fills me with dread. I know I’m already quite lean, probably too lean, but I still feel like I need to lose more, or at least keep it off. Sometimes, I find myself just totally losing control around food, especially when I'm stressed from work. I'll eat way too much, too fast, and then I just feel this immense guilt and shame. I try to compensate, if I can, to "undo" it. It's become a cycle that’s really hard to break, and it's starting to affect my focus, even at the plant."

D021-D022_h019.question:

I'll eat a large quantity of food, very quickly, only to feel overwhelmed by guilt and a desperate need to undo it. It’s a vicious cycle, and frankly, it’s exhausting. D021-D022_h021.question: "*Sighs*... I don't know, it's just... a lot. The studio, the rehearsals, the pressure. I've been so careful with what I eat, probably for the past year or so. I try to skip meals when I can, especially if I feel like I ate too much the day before. Breakfast is usually a no-go, and sometimes lunch too if I’m really feeling… heavy.     C. Bulimia Nervosa

D021-D022_h022.question:
"Doc, thanks for seeing me. It's… tough to talk about. For the past few months, things have felt out of whack. I used to just eat whatever, but now I’m meticulously counting every single calorie, trying to keep it as low as possible. I know it’s messed up, but it feels like the only way to get rid of the feeling, to stop the weight from creeping back on. I usually just try to forget it happened, tell myself it won't happen again. It's been going on like this for about six months now. I'm just trying to feel like myself again, you know?"

D021-D022_h023.question: "It's been... well, a good six months now, maybe a bit more, that things have felt off. My wife, bless her heart, she’s noticed I’ve been rather particular about what I eat.     D. Anorexia Nervosa
